differences.what: massing: the four-storey red front on the street line under its deep bracketed cornice, the long buff common-brick west flank and rear range behind it, its parapet under the front's cornice and the rear stepping down, as the photograph shows them (camera residuals 3.4 px RMS)

the front's openings: the third storey's round-headed lights and the fourth storey's square-headed ones, in the columns the photograph shows; the front's east column falls where the front turns away from this camera behind the tree's crown

the cornice at the far (north-east) corner stands about 0.6 m off the photograph, the cornice's own depth; and the red brick returns about 0.7 m onto the west flank in the photograph where the build turns buff at the corner

the two-storey dark timber-and-glass bays on the west flank: the 1911 sheet draws no projection on that wall (T-3782 read it at full size and found the only one on the east wall), so they are taken as a later addition and not built into 1904
the lower two storeys, the door and its hood (photograph 222 reads them), and 215 and 217: behind the trees
tone: the front reads a brighter red in the photograph (2009 paint or cleaning is possible); the same red pressed brick

the date: a 2009 photograph of the surviving house, 105 years after the scene, is evidence of 2009 (AGENTS.md rule 11); the copper's green patina, the window grilles, the fence and the planting are 2009's and are not copied into 1904

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
